metadata.scope: Exhaustive SOTA pattern extraction; settings.json env vars + 175+ env, hooks, MCP, permissions, agents, commands, skills, memory, git workflow, review/audit, harness primitives
metadata.rules: Zero self-invention. Every recommendation cites primary source. Ambiguous patterns marked STATUS:ambiguous.

patterns.name: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H — 1-hour prompt cache TTL
patterns.what: Opt into 1-hour prompt cache TTL (replaces the deprecated ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK). Reduces re-cost of stable system prompt + CLAUDE.md across short-window sessions.
patterns.where: settings.json env block, user or project scope. ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1.

patterns.name: FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M — force 5-minute cache TTL
patterns.what: Force a 5-minute prompt cache TTL — useful when 1H opt-in is not enabled but you want a deterministic short-window cache.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Mutually exclusive with ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H. Choose one based on session length pattern.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB — defense-in-depth credential scrub
patterns.what: Set to 1 to strip Anthropic and cloud-provider credentials from subprocess environments (Bash tool, hooks, MCP stdio servers). Defense-in-depth when subprocesses should not inherit API keys (v2.1.83).
patterns.applied_evidence: Z:/claude-sota/.claude/settings.json:69 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=0 (current setting opts OUT of scrub)
patterns.leverage: high (security) — current 0 setting may warrant review

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SCRIPT_CAPS — per-script invocation limit JSON
patterns.what: JSON object limiting how many times specific scripts may be invoked per session when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set. Substring-matched. Defense-in-depth, not enforced through xargs/find -exec fan-out.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE — Perforce write protection
patterns.what: Set to 1 to enable Perforce-aware write protection. Edit/Write/NotebookEdit fail with p4 edit hint when target lacks owner-write bit (v2.1.98).
patterns.where: settings.json env. Skip unless using Perforce.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS — strip default git/PR system prompt
patterns.what: Strips CC's built-in git/PR workflow text + git status snapshot from the system prompt. Saves ~200-500 tokens/turn × every prompt × fleet. Safe when project has stricter custom commit discipline.
patterns.where: settings.json env. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1. Also configurable via includeGitInstructions:false.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER — disable cache-breaking version header
patterns.citation: shan repo does NOT cite this directly; user's local note at Z:/claude-sota/.claude/settings.json:34 cites motiful/cc-cache-audit + claude-code-router PR #1220 + CLIProxyAPI #1592
patterns.what: Set to 0 to disable CC v2.1.69+ injection of x-anthropic-billing-header (cc_version=2.1.<3-char-sha256-hash>) into the system prompt. Restores prompt-caching across CC version bumps (~85% cost reduction in motiful audit).
patterns.applied_status: ADOPTED (not from shan, but from upstream sources)
patterns.note: STATUS: not_in_shan_repo — this is a separately-discovered pattern, listed for completeness. Not from this extraction's primary source.

patterns.name: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto:N — MCP tool description deferral
patterns.what: Tunes the MCP tool-search auto-defer threshold by context-window percentage. auto:5 = defer when descriptions exceed 5% of context (more aggressive than default ~10%). Saves ~10-20K tokens/turn when many MCP tools registered.
patterns.leverage: high (cost) for fleets with 10+ MCP servers

patterns.name: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS — MCP output cap
patterns.what: Default 25000 tokens per MCP tool response; warning displayed when output exceeds 10000.

patterns.name: MCP_TIMEOUT / MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT — startup vs per-call
patterns.what: MCP_TIMEOUT controls startup/connection timeout; MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT controls per-tool execution timeout. Separate dials.

patterns.name: MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING — skip MCP connect wait in -p mode
patterns.what: Set to true in -p mode to skip MCP connection wait entirely. Bounds --mcp-config server connections at 5s instead of blocking on slowest server (v2.1.89).
patterns.where: settings.json env, BUT scoped to specific -p call sites only (not ambient — would race MCP startup for every -p call expecting MCP-backed context).
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:45 _comment_mcp_nonblocking_scoped — scoped to tools/loop7h_remediation_cron.ps1 only per Wave 19 fire-5

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT — isolated child-process subagents
patterns.what: Set to 1 to enable forked subagents on external builds. Forked subagents run in an isolated child process instead of sharing the main agent's context. Also remaps /fork from session-branch to subagent-spawn.
patterns.leverage: high (true context isolation, not just window split)

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS — multi-session orchestration
patterns.what: Enable experimental Agent Teams: multiple independent Claude Code sessions coordinating via shared task list. Each teammate gets full context window (CLAUDE.md, MCP, skills auto-loaded). Differs from subagents (context fork) — true multi-session with tmux/iTerm2 split panes.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER — flicker-free alt-screen rendering
patterns.what: Enable flicker-free alt-screen rendering (v2.1.88). Eliminates visual flicker during fullscreen redraws.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONSTREAMING_FALLBACK — prevent duplicate tool execution
patterns.what: Set to 1 to disable the non-streaming fallback when streaming request fails mid-stream. Streaming errors propagate to retry layer instead. Fixes proxy/gateway-induced duplicate tool execution (v2.1.83).
patterns.leverage: medium-high (reliability when behind proxy — claude-sota uses CCC at 9327)

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING — token-level tool streaming
patterns.what: Enable fine-grained tool streaming. Provides incremental tool-input updates rather than waiting for full tool block.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY — parallel read-only tool calls
patterns.what: Max parallel read-only tools (default 10). Cap on Read/Grep/Glob/WebSearch concurrency.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS — per-response cap
patterns.what: Max output tokens per response. Default 32000 (64000 for Opus 4.6 v2.1.77). Upper bound 64000 (128000 for Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 v2.1.77). Cap is a CEILING — cost only paid on actually-emitted tokens.
patterns.where: settings.json env. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=128000 for max ceiling on Opus/Sonnet 4.6.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE — early auto-compact threshold
patterns.what: Auto-compact threshold percentage (1-100). Default ~95%. Set lower (e.g., 50, 70, 80) to trigger compaction earlier and avoid mid-task context exhaustion.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW — decouple compact threshold from context size
patterns.what: Override the context capacity in tokens used for auto-compaction calculations. Defaults to model context window (200K standard, 1M for extended). Set lower (e.g., 500000) on a 1M model to treat as 500K for compaction. Decouples compaction threshold from /context's used_percentage.
patterns.applied_evidence: Not present in settings.json env; running opus[1m] without explicit window cap

patterns.name: DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC
patterns.what: DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1 disables flavor text and non-essential model calls (UNVERIFIED in official docs per shan note). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 is the equivalent of setting DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER + DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND + DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING + DISABLE_TELEMETRY together.
patterns.applied_evidence: Not present (telemetry currently enabled at line 53)
patterns.note: STATUS: ambiguous on DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS — shan flags it as 'not in official docs — unverified'.

patterns.name: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES / OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS — verbose OTel content
patterns.what: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1 emits full API request/response bodies to OTel (v2.1.111). OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 includes user_system_prompt in LLM request spans (v2.1.121). Both off by default for privacy.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Use only when you control the OTel collector.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:78 OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1; lines for raw bodies / prompts missing

patterns.name: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS — include tool_parameters in OTel events
patterns.what: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 includes tool_parameters in OpenTelemetry events. Omitted by default for privacy (v2.1.85).

patterns.name: CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG / CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS — stalled-stream guards
patterns.what: CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG=1 force-enables byte-level streaming idle watchdog (5min minimum). CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=N controls timeout. Two watchdogs apply: byte-level (no bytes) and event-level (no SSE events, default 90s).
patterns.where: settings.json env. Increase event timeout if long-running tools or slow networks cause premature timeouts.

patterns.name: API_TIMEOUT_MS / CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES — extend network resilience
patterns.what: API_TIMEOUT_MS default 600000 (10 min). CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES default 10.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Raise for unstable connections / behind proxies.

patterns.name: BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS / BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS / BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH
patterns.what: BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = default per-bash timeout (no model-set timeout). BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS = absolute upper bound. BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH = max captured stdout/stderr.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Output length is a CEILING — cost only on emitted bytes.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR — persist cwd across bash calls
patterns.what: Keep cwd between bash calls (1 to enable). Default: each bash call starts in project root.

patterns.name: SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET — slash command output character budget
patterns.what: Character budget for slash command tool output. Default 15000 — skill descriptions are loaded into context up to this budget. In large monorepos with many skills, may hit limit and exclude skills.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Raise to fit more skills (e.g., 30000).

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL — global subagent model override
patterns.what: Override model for subagents (e.g., haiku, sonnet). Has TOP priority over agent frontmatter — setting overrides per-agent declarations.
patterns.where: settings.json env. WARNING: Will override declared model: in agent frontmatter.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:42 _comment_subagent_model_removed_2026_04_30 — removed because env had top priority and overrode 3 agents that explicitly declared model: sonnet
patterns.leverage: high (cost) — keep removed unless you need fleet-wide override

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID — multi-session shared task collaboration
patterns.what: Task list ID for cross-session/cross-agent task coordination. All sessions sharing same ID see task updates in real-time. Enables parallel workstreams and session resumption.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA / CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR — relocate caches
patterns.what: Override tmp/plugin paths. CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR appends /claude/. CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR overrides plugins root. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA per-plugin data dir.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Relocate to fast/large drive.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — relocate ~/.claude home
patterns.what: Custom config directory (overrides default ~/.claude).
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:9-10 HOME and USERPROFILE both pinned to Z:\claude-sota

patterns.name: DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT vs DISABLE_COMPACT
patterns.what: DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 disables only automatic compaction (manual /compact still works). DISABLE_COMPACT=1 disables both.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Avoid both unless using strategic-compact pattern with explicit gates.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_HIDE_CWD — hide cwd in startup banner
patterns.what: Set to 1 to hide cwd in CC startup logo banner. Useful in screen recordings, demos, shared sessions where path leaks info (v2.1.119).

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY — kill feedback survey prompts
patterns.what: Disable feedback survey prompts (1 to disable).

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY — idle-session recap
patterns.what: Pairs with awaySummaryEnabled. Generates summary when user returns after idle.

patterns.name: Permission rule prefixes: //, ~/, /, ./
patterns.what: Permission rules for Read/Edit/Write support gitignore-style prefixes: // (absolute), ~/ (home), / (project root), ./ or none (relative). Distinct from sandbox.filesystem prefixes which use // / ~/ / ./ slightly differently — sandbox uses / for absolute, ~/ for home, ./ for relative.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json uses Write(Z:/...) absolute Windows paths — works but redundant with project-root prefix

patterns.name: Bash wildcard word-boundary semantics
patterns.what: Bash(ls *) matches 'ls -la' but NOT 'lsof' (space before *). Bash(ls*) matches both. Bash(*) equivalent to Bash. Legacy :* suffix syntax (e.g., Bash(npm:*)) deprecated; use ' *' instead.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json uses 'Bash(npm view *)' style — current SOTA spacing

patterns.name: Permission deny rules have highest precedence
patterns.what: Deny rules have highest safety precedence and cannot be overridden by lower-priority allow/ask. Evaluation order: deny → ask → allow. First matching rule wins.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:175-200 deny block is comprehensive (rm -rf, force push, branch deletion, etc.)

patterns.name: Agent(name) permission syntax — restrict spawnable subagents
patterns.what: Permission rules support Agent(name) for restricting which subagents can be spawned. Older Task(name) alias still works.
patterns.where: settings.json permissions.allow/deny. Agent(*) for all, Agent(specific-name) for one.

patterns.name: additionalDirectories — extend Claude's reach beyond cwd
patterns.what: Extra directories Claude can access. Use sparingly — broadens blast radius.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:204-210 includes Z:/repos/deps/, Z:/claude/, Z:/tools/, Z:/venvs/claude/, Z:/repos/

patterns.name: skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt — skip bypass-mode confirmation
patterns.what: Skip the confirmation prompt shown before entering bypassPermissions mode. IGNORED in shared project settings (.claude/settings.json) to prevent untrusted repos from auto-bypassing — only honored in user-scope settings.
patterns.leverage: low-medium (UX, but only works at user scope)

patterns.name: defaultMode: bypassPermissions / acceptEdits / auto / plan
patterns.what: Permission modes: default (prompts), acceptEdits (auto-accept edits), dontAsk (auto-deny unless allowed), bypassPermissions (skip checks; protected paths still prompt — .git, .claude, .vscode), auto (background classifier auto-approves read-only + edits, sends rest through safety check, 3-consecutive/20-total block fallback, /Shift+Tab cycle), plan (read-only).

patterns.name: autoMode classifier configuration
patterns.what: Customize what auto-mode classifier blocks/allows. Object with environment (trusted infra strings), allow (exceptions), soft_deny (block rules) — all arrays of prose. NOT read from .claude/settings.json (project) to prevent repo injection. allow/soft_deny REPLACES default list unless $defaults sentinel included. claude auto-mode defaults to view built-ins.
patterns.where: User/local/managed settings only. Use to encode trusted internal infra and explicit denials.
patterns.leverage: high (workflow accuracy if using auto mode)

patterns.name: Hook event taxonomy — 25+ event types
patterns.what: Complete hook event taxonomy demonstrated in shan repo: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Setup, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, ConfigChange, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, InstructionsLoaded, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, StopFailure, CwdChanged, FileChanged, PermissionDenied. shan uses ONE python dispatcher per event with statusMessage discriminator.
patterns.where: settings.json hooks.<EventName>[].hooks[]. Each hook: type:command, command, timeout (ms), async (boolean), once (boolean for SessionStart/PreCompact/SessionEnd), statusMessage, matcher (regex for FileChanged etc).
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota uses many events but missing: PermissionRequest (different shape), Notification, TaskCreated, ConfigChange (has it), TeammateIdle, Setup, FileChanged, PermissionDenied, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, CwdChanged, WorktreeCreate. Event matrix coverage ~60%.

patterns.name: Hook 'once' field — fire-once-per-session events
patterns.what: once:true on hook entry fires the hook only once per session (not per event repeat). Useful for SessionStart/PreCompact/SessionEnd boundary events.
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota Stop/SessionStart hooks lack 'once' — fires every iteration
patterns.leverage: medium (avoid duplicate writes from same session)

patterns.name: Hook 'matcher' field — pattern-scope hooks
patterns.what: matcher field scopes a hook to specific tool names or file patterns. shan uses matcher pipe-separated regex for FileChanged. claude-sota uses matcher 'Edit|Write|MultiEdit', 'Bash', 'Agent', 'ExitPlanMode' to narrow PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks.

patterns.name: Hook 'if' field — conditional bash-pattern firing
patterns.what: Per-hook 'if' field constrains a hook to fire only when a specific bash-pattern matches inside a Bash matcher. Used for git-commit-only hooks while still in the broad Bash matcher group. NOT documented in shan repo's hook examples but is in claude-sota current usage.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json — 30+ uses of 'if' for git commit/push/merge
patterns.note: STATUS: not_in_shan_repo — claude-sota uses this; shan does not demonstrate. May be CC-builtin via hook schema.

patterns.name: Hook 'mcp_tool' type — direct MCP tool invocation in hooks (v2.1.118)
patterns.what: CC v2.1.118+ supports type:mcp_tool hook entries that directly invoke an MCP tool server.tool with input object (supports ${tool_input.command} interpolation). Replaces shell-out to MCP — runs in same process. Used in claude-sota for Graphiti commit ingestion.
patterns.where: settings.json hooks: { type: 'mcp_tool', server: '...', tool: '...', input: {...}, if: '...', timeout: 15, statusMessage: '...' }.
patterns.note: STATUS: not_in_shan_repo — claude-sota uses; shan repo uses only type:command. Listed here per CC v2.1.118 changelog.

patterns.name: type:'prompt' hooks (v2.1.92+) — cheap inline LLM validation
patterns.citation: User CLAUDE.md V442 P1 Runtime: 'type: prompt hooks supported (CC v2.1.92+): use model: haiku for cheap inline validation. Events: Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse.'
patterns.what: Hook with type:prompt fires a model invocation as the hook body — use model:haiku for cheap inline validation. Events restricted to Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse.
patterns.where: settings.json hooks.<event>[].hooks[]: { type: 'prompt', prompt: '...', model: 'haiku', timeout: ms }.
patterns.applied_evidence: Not in shan repo or claude-sota settings
patterns.leverage: very high (cheap inline LLM gates without shell-out latency)
patterns.note: STATUS: not_in_shan_repo — sourced from user's CLAUDE.md ref to pro-workflow hooks.json:24-50; included as ambient SOTA pattern even though not in shan.

patterns.name: Hook execution order — guardrail-first segregation
patterns.citation: User rules system-platform.md (Hook Execution Order); Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan does NOT explicitly document order-segregation but uses single-dispatcher pattern.
patterns.what: PreToolUse hooks should be ordered: (1) GUARDRAILS (blocking — exit 2 to deny), (2) CONTEXT (non-blocking inject), (3) OBSERVABILITY (non-blocking async). Settings.json array position determines order. Stop hooks: quality gates run blocking before async observers.
patterns.applied_status: ADOPTED in claude-sota (codified in user rules)
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json PreToolUse order: T1 gate → secret_scan_guard → gitnexus_pre_edit → intent_gate (claude-sota); shan uses single python dispatcher per event
patterns.note: STATUS: ambiguous — shan does NOT codify this; pattern is upstream agno AG-1 + user V449.

patterns.name: alwaysLoad:true — MCP per-server tool loading exemption
patterns.what: By default MCP tool definitions are deferred (loaded on demand via tool search). Set alwaysLoad:true on individual MCP server entry in .mcp.json (or inline mcpServers) to load all tools upfront at session start regardless of ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH. Available on all server types; CC v2.1.121+. MCP server can also mark individual tools always-loaded by including 'anthropic/alwaysLoad':true in tool _meta. Use only for tools needed every turn — context cost.
patterns.applied_evidence: .mcp.json:35 only gitnexus has alwaysLoad:true; graphiti/github/repomix/mcp-memory had alwaysLoad REMOVED in token-reduction-pass S1

patterns.name: Environment variable expansion in .mcp.json — ${VAR_NAME}
patterns.what: Use environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys. Pattern: "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}".
patterns.where: .mcp.json server config — env, args, url all support ${VAR}.
patterns.applied_evidence: .mcp.json — 12+ uses of ${VAR}: GITHUB_TOKEN, CONTEXT7_API_KEY, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.

patterns.name: MCP server scope precedence: Subagent > Project > User
patterns.what: Three MCP scopes: Subagent (agent frontmatter mcpServers field) → Project (.mcp.json at repo root) → User (~/.claude.json mcpServers key). Subagent overrides project overrides user.
patterns.where: Choose scope based on share intent: team-shared vs personal vs agent-specific.
patterns.applied_evidence: .mcp.json at project root; agent files reference subagent-scoped MCP

patterns.name: stdio vs http MCP server types
patterns.what: stdio (spawns local process via npx/python/binary) vs http (connects to remote URL endpoint, HTTP/SSE).
patterns.where: .mcp.json server.type. Use http when there's a stable hosted endpoint (DeepWiki, Context7); stdio for local tools.
patterns.applied_status: ADOPTED — 4 http servers (context7, deepwiki, langfuse, claude_ai_Google_Drive)

patterns.name: OAuth via RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata (v2.1.111)
patterns.what: MCP servers authenticating via OAuth follow RFC 9728 for protected-resource metadata discovery. Compliant servers expose authorization endpoints under /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Claude Code completes OAuth flow automatically — no manual apiKeyHelper or headersHelper script required for spec-conformant servers.

patterns.name: headersHelper script with CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME / _URL env
patterns.what: headersHelper scripts receive CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL env vars (v2.1.85), enabling server-specific authentication header generation in a single shared helper.
patterns.where: .mcp.json mcpServers.<name>.headersHelper. Use for token-scoped per-server auth.
patterns.leverage: low-medium (operational hygiene if running multiple authed servers)

patterns.name: sandbox.enabled / failIfUnavailable — strict sandboxing
patterns.what: sandbox.enabled:true enables bash sandboxing. failIfUnavailable:true exits with error when sandbox cannot start (instead of running unsandboxed). For enterprise policies requiring strict sandboxing (v2.1.83). allowUnsandboxedCommands:false disables dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch entirely.

patterns.name: sandbox.network.deniedDomains — sandbox network deny
patterns.what: Network domain denylist for bash sandbox. Takes precedence over wildcards in allowedDomains. Supports glob patterns (e.g., '*.example.com') (v2.1.113).
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:1031-1037 — webhook.site, ngrok, requestbin denied. No effect since sandbox is off.

patterns.name: sandbox.filesystem.allowRead/denyRead/allowWrite/denyWrite
patterns.what: Sandbox filesystem allow/deny lists. Arrays MERGED across all settings scopes (not replaced). Also merged with paths from Edit(...)/Read(...) permission rules. Path prefix conventions: /, ~/, ./ — NOTE these differ from Read/Edit permission rules (which use // for absolute, / for project).

patterns.name: Agent frontmatter — 16 fields
patterns.what: Subagent frontmatter (16 fields): name (required), description (required), tools, disallowedTools, model (sonnet/opus/haiku/full ID/inherit; default inherit), permissionMode (default/acceptEdits/auto/dontAsk/bypassPermissions/plan), maxTurns, skills (preload list), mcpServers (server names or inline configs), hooks, memory (user/project/local), background (boolean), effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max), isolation ('worktree' for temp git worktree), initialPrompt (auto-submitted as first user turn), color (red/blue/green/yellow/purple/orange/pink/cyan).
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota uses these fields broadly but coverage of `initialPrompt`, `background`, `isolation:worktree` is uneven across agents

patterns.name: Agent skill preloading — full content injection
patterns.what: skills: list in agent frontmatter preloads named skills' FULL content (not just made available) into agent's startup context. Differs from main-conversation skills (description-only loaded by default). Subagent-only behavior.
patterns.applied_evidence: Agents in claude-sota define skills field but full coverage uneven

patterns.name: Agent memory: user/project/local — persistent learning
patterns.what: v2.1.33+ — memory: frontmatter gives subagent persistent markdown knowledge store. user (~/.claude/agent-memory/<name>/, no VC, cross-project), project (.claude/agent-memory/<name>/, VC, team-shared), local (.claude/agent-memory-local/<name>/, no VC, personal). On startup: first 200 lines of MEMORY.md injected into system prompt. Read/Write/Edit auto-enabled. If MEMORY.md > 200 lines, agent moves details to topic-specific files.
patterns.applied_status: PARTIAL — autoMemoryDirectory set but agent memory frontmatter coverage unknown

patterns.name: Agent isolation:worktree — temporary git worktree
patterns.what: isolation:'worktree' runs subagent in temp git worktree (auto-cleaned if no changes). Combine with worktree.symlinkDirectories / worktree.sparsePaths in settings.json for fast startup.
patterns.applied_status: PARTIAL — settings.json has symlinkDirectories but no sparsePaths

patterns.name: Agent initialPrompt — auto-submitted first user turn
patterns.what: initialPrompt: auto-submitted as first user turn when agent runs as MAIN session agent (via --agent or agent setting). Commands and skills are processed. Prepended to any user-provided prompt.

patterns.name: Built-in subagents: general-purpose / Explore / Plan / statusline-setup / claude-code-guide
patterns.what: 5 built-in subagents: general-purpose (inherit, all tools), Explore (haiku, read-only — fast codebase search), Plan (inherit, read-only — pre-planning research), statusline-setup (sonnet), claude-code-guide (haiku — Claude Code docs Q&A).
patterns.where: Available out of the box. Spawn via Agent(Explore, ...) etc.
patterns.leverage: high (Explore for code search is the SOTA recall route)

patterns.name: Command frontmatter — 15 fields
patterns.what: Slash command frontmatter (15 fields): name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments (named positional for $name substitution), disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, paths (glob — limit auto-load to matching files), allowed-tools, model, effort, context (set 'fork' for isolated subagent context), agent (subagent type when fork; default general-purpose), shell (bash/powershell), hooks (lifecycle hooks scoped to this command).

patterns.name: Command context:fork — isolated subagent context
patterns.what: Set context:fork on a command to run it in an isolated subagent context. Pair with agent: <subagent-type> (default general-purpose). Like spawning a subagent but invoked as /command.

patterns.name: Built-in /effort command — direct effort level control
patterns.what: /effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max|auto sets model effort directly (v2.1.76+). Slider via /model UI ← →. Persists via effortLevel key.

patterns.name: Built-in /branch — fork conversation at point
patterns.what: /branch [name] (alias /fork) creates a branch of current conversation at this point. When CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT is set, /fork instead spawns a forked subagent (no longer alias).
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota has CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1 → /fork now spawns subagent

patterns.name: Built-in /ultrareview — multi-agent cloud-sandbox PR review
patterns.what: /ultrareview [PR] runs deep, multi-agent code review of given PR in cloud sandbox. Produces structured review with prioritized findings; complements local /review.
patterns.where: Built-in. Requires Claude Code on the web access.

patterns.name: Built-in /autofix-pr — CI-watching auto-fix loop
patterns.what: /autofix-pr [prompt] spawns Claude Code on the web session that watches current branch's PR and pushes fixes when CI fails or reviewers comment. Detects open PR via gh pr view. Requires gh CLI.

patterns.name: Built-in /team-onboarding — 30-day usage analysis → onboarding
patterns.what: /team-onboarding generates team onboarding guide from CC usage history (sessions, commands, MCP usage, past 30 days).

patterns.name: Built-in /insights — session analysis report
patterns.what: /insights generates report analyzing CC sessions: project areas, interaction patterns, friction points.

patterns.name: Built-in /security-review — pending-changes vuln scan
patterns.what: /security-review analyzes pending changes on current branch for security vulnerabilities. Reviews git diff and identifies injection, auth, data exposure risks.

patterns.name: Skill frontmatter — 15 fields
patterns.what: Skill frontmatter (15 fields): name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments (named positional), disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, model, effort, context (fork), agent (when forking), hooks, paths (glob — limit auto-activation), shell. when_to_use is appended to description in skill listing; counts toward 1,536-char cap.
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota has 207 skills; uneven adoption of paths/when_to_use

patterns.name: Skill paths: lazy auto-activation by file glob
patterns.what: paths: glob patterns limit when skill auto-activates. Comma-separated string or YAML list. Claude loads skill ONLY when working with matching files. Reduces cold-start context.
patterns.applied_evidence: shan CLAUDE.md:95 confirms .claude/rules/*.md with paths: are lazy-loaded only when Claude touches matching files

patterns.name: Skill description char cap — 1,536 characters
patterns.what: description + when_to_use combined cap at 1,536 characters per skill. Verbose descriptions waste context budget.

patterns.name: user-invocable:false — agent-preload-only skills
patterns.what: user-invocable:false hides skill from / menu — becomes background knowledge only, intended for agent preloading via skills: frontmatter. Auto-discovery still works via description match unless disable-model-invocation:true also set.
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota has skillOverrides:'name-only' for some — different mechanism

patterns.name: Skills nested-directory automatic discovery
patterns.what: Skills automatically discovered from nested .claude/skills/ when working with files in those subdirectories. Differs from CLAUDE.md (ancestor-loaded). Description loaded; full content lazy-loaded on invocation.

patterns.name: Skill priority: Enterprise > User > Project (name conflict resolution)
patterns.what: When skills share names: Enterprise > Personal (~/.claude/skills/) > Project (.claude/skills/). Plugin skills use plugin-name:skill-name namespace — no conflict.
patterns.where: Plan skill name namespace strategy. Use plugin namespace for shared catalogs.

patterns.name: CLAUDE.md ancestor (UP) loading vs descendant (DOWN) lazy loading
patterns.what: CLAUDE.md walks UP directory tree from cwd at startup (all ancestors loaded immediately). Descendant CLAUDE.md files load LAZILY when Claude reads files in those subdirs. Siblings NEVER load. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is global ancestor for all sessions.
patterns.where: Project structure: place shared conventions in root CLAUDE.md; component-specific in subdir CLAUDE.md.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 — load CLAUDE.md from --add-dir paths
patterns.what: Enable additional directory CLAUDE.md loading. Without this, --add-dir / additionalDirectories paths do NOT contribute their CLAUDE.md to context.
patterns.where: Shell startup env. Required when using additionalDirectories with CLAUDE.md content.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json env block does not include this — additionalDirectories has 5 entries; no CLAUDE.md loading from those
patterns.leverage: medium-high (depending on whether deps/ has CLAUDE.md worth loading)

patterns.name: claudeMdExcludes — exclude path globs from CLAUDE.md discovery
patterns.citation: Z:/claude-sota/.claude/settings.json:1060-1069 (in-use); not explicitly cited in shan claude-settings.md @ HEAD 64fffd53
patterns.what: Exclude globs from CLAUDE.md walking — node_modules, .venv, archived, etc. Avoid loading 1000s of vendored CLAUDE.mds.
patterns.note: STATUS: ambiguous — exists in JSON schema but shan repo's claude-settings.md does not document; sourced from claude-sota's live config.

patterns.name: autoMemoryEnabled / autoMemoryDirectory
patterns.what: autoMemoryDirectory: custom directory for auto-memory storage (~/-expanded). NOT accepted in project settings (.claude/settings.json) to prevent redirecting writes to sensitive locations. Accepted from policy/local/user.
patterns.where: User/local settings only. Pair with autoMemoryEnabled.

patterns.name: CLAUDE.local.md — personal git-ignored memory
patterns.what: CLAUDE.local.md for personal preferences. Add to .gitignore for instructions that shouldn't be shared with team.

patterns.name: Workflow Best Practices: <200 lines/CLAUDE.md, /compact at 50%
patterns.what: Shan repo's own working rules: keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines per file for reliable adherence; use commands for workflows instead of standalone agents; create feature-specific subagents with skills (progressive disclosure) not general-purpose agents; perform manual /compact at ~50% context; start with plan mode for complex tasks; use human-gated task list workflow; break subtasks small enough to complete in <50% context.
patterns.where: Discipline rules. Mostly enforce via reading habits + auto-compact threshold.
patterns.applied_status: PARTIALLY (auto-compact at 70%, CLAUDE.md size discipline uneven)
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:66 — autocompact at 70% (more conservative than 50% manual but later than recommended)

patterns.name: extraKnownMarketplaces — add custom plugin marketplaces
patterns.what: Project-scope plugin marketplaces. Source types: github, git, directory, hostPattern, settings (inline), url, npm, file. Use 'settings' source to declare inline plugins without hosted marketplace.

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL — wait for plugins before first query
patterns.what: Wait for plugin install to complete before first query (1 to enable). Pair with CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS.
patterns.where: settings.json env. Use in CI / setup scripts.
patterns.applied_evidence: Not present — plugins install async by default

patterns.name: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE — offline-resilient cache
patterns.what: Set 1 to keep existing marketplace cache when git pull fails (vs wiping and re-cloning). Useful in offline/airgapped environments.

patterns.name: spinnerVerbs / spinnerTipsOverride — custom UX
patterns.what: spinnerVerbs:{mode:'append'|'replace', verbs:[...]} customizes spinner verb pool (179 built-in). spinnerTipsOverride:{tips:[], excludeDefault:true} replaces or merges spinner tips.

patterns.name: statusLine.command + refreshInterval
patterns.what: statusLine.command runs shell on event-driven updates; refreshInterval re-runs every N seconds (min 1) for time-based / background-update display. Receives JSON on stdin: model, cwd, workspace, cost, context_window, rate_limits, session_id, transcript_path, version, output_style, vim, agent, effort, thinking, worktree, etc.

patterns.name: fileSuggestion.command — custom @ autocomplete
patterns.what: fileSuggestion script receives JSON on stdin ({"query":"src/comp"}) and outputs up to 15 file paths (one per line). Override @ file autocomplete behavior.

patterns.name: outputStyle: Explanatory / Concise / etc
patterns.what: Output style preset (e.g., 'Explanatory'). Affects tone, verbosity, explanation depth, emoji usage.

patterns.name: cleanupPeriodDays — startup cleanup sweep
patterns.what: Age cutoff for startup cleanup sweep (min 1, default 30). Inactive session transcripts and orphaned subagent worktrees deleted. v2.1.117+ also covers ~/.claude/tasks/, ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/, ~/.claude/backups/. Setting 0 rejected.

patterns.name: apiKeyHelper — dynamic auth token script
patterns.what: Shell script path that outputs auth token (sent as X-Api-Key). Pair with CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS for refresh interval.
patterns.where: settings.json apiKeyHelper. Use for short-lived tokens / rotated credentials.
patterns.applied_evidence: settings.json:26 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN static (CCC fleet token, not Anthropic — safe per comment)

patterns.name: forceLoginMethod / forceLoginOrgUUID — restrict login source
patterns.what: forceLoginMethod restricts login to 'claudeai' or 'console'. forceLoginOrgUUID requires login to belong to specific org UUID(s). Empty array fails closed.
patterns.leverage: low for solo, high for enterprise

patterns.name: attribution.commit / attribution.pr / prUrlTemplate
patterns.what: attribution.commit (git trailer text), attribution.pr (PR description text). prUrlTemplate (v2.1.119) — URL template controlling 'PR' badge link in commit attribution. Supports placeholders {host}, {owner}, {repo}, {number}. For self-hosted GitLab/Bitbucket. Set empty string to hide attribution.

patterns.name: --worktree (-w) — start in isolated git worktree
patterns.what: Start Claude in isolated git worktree branched from HEAD. Pair with worktree.symlinkDirectories / sparsePaths for fast startup in monorepos.

patterns.name: --from-pr <NUMBER|URL> — resume sessions linked to a PR
patterns.what: Resume sessions linked to a specific GitHub PR.

patterns.name: --fork-session — new session ID on resume/continue
patterns.what: Create new session ID when resuming (use with --resume or --continue). Differs from --session-id which sets explicit UUID.

patterns.name: --max-budget-usd <AMOUNT> / --max-turns — print-mode budget caps
patterns.what: --max-budget-usd: max dollar amount before stopping (print mode only). --max-turns: limit agentic turns (print mode only).
patterns.where: CLI flag for headless / scripted runs.

patterns.name: --init / --init-only / --maintenance — lifecycle hook runners
patterns.what: --init runs initialization hooks then enters interactive. --init-only runs hooks and exits (no session). --maintenance runs maintenance hooks and exits.
patterns.where: CLI flag. Use --init-only / --maintenance in scheduled tasks for hook-driven cleanup.
patterns.applied_evidence: Not used in tools/loop crons currently

patterns.name: --strict-mcp-config — only --mcp-config servers, ignore others
patterns.what: Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config; ignore project .mcp.json and user mcpServers.
patterns.where: CLI flag for hermetic test/eval runs.

patterns.name: --setting-sources <user,project,local> — selective scope load
patterns.what: Comma-separated list of which scopes to load. user, project, local. Useful for testing project-only behavior or hermetic runs.

patterns.name: Command → Agent → Skill orchestration architecture
patterns.what: Layered orchestration pattern: Command (entry point, user interaction) → Agent (autonomous data fetch with preloaded skill — 'agent skill') → Skill (output generation, invoked directly via Skill tool). Two distinct skill patterns: agent skills (preloaded full content) vs skills (description-loaded, invoked on-demand). Resolution order when multiple match same intent: Skill (inline, no overhead) > Agent (separate context) > Command (never auto-invoked).
patterns.where: Project structure: .claude/commands/<name>.md (orchestrator) → .claude/agents/<name>.md (autonomous worker w/ skills:[<preload>]) → .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (output / domain knowledge).
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota has commands, agents, skills but the strict 3-layer pattern is not uniformly enforced

patterns.name: Subagents cannot invoke subagents via bash; use Agent tool
patterns.what: Subagents CANNOT invoke other subagents via bash commands. Use the Agent tool (renamed from Task in v2.1.63; Task() still works as alias). Be explicit about tool usage in subagent definitions; avoid vague terms like 'launch' that could be misinterpreted as bash commands. Pattern: Agent(subagent_type='agent-name', description='...', prompt='...', model='haiku').

patterns.name: Plain modular system prompt — ~269 base tokens + 110+ conditional fragments
patterns.what: CLI uses modular system prompt: ~269-token base + 110+ conditional fragments (tools, coding guidelines, safety, env context, project context — CLAUDE.md, MCP descriptions, plan/explore prompts, security review fragment ~2,610 tokens conditional). SDK default is minimal — requires `claude_code` preset to match.
patterns.where: Implication: every settings.json env that disables a fragment (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS, CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE, etc.) directly cuts tokens off the every-turn baseline.
patterns.applied_evidence: Drives SET-006 (disable git instructions) adoption rationale

patterns.name: Output quality = f(effective context, model capability, iteration loop)
patterns.what: For non-trivial tasks, quality = f(effective context, model capability, iteration loop). User controls a sliver of effective context; harness controls the rest + iteration loop entirely. 10 architectural capabilities (context isolation, harness-enforced tool restrictions, lazy-loaded rules/memory, hooks, model routing, parallelism, cross-session persistence, modular system prompt, skill preloading, permission classification) operate at layers prompts cannot reach.
patterns.applied_evidence: Aligns with user's V442 'Five Fundamental Truths' rules

patterns.name: Separate commits per file (shan repo own rule)
patterns.what: When committing changes, create SEPARATE commits per file. Do NOT bundle multiple file changes into single commit. Each file gets own commit with descriptive message specific to that file's changes. Makes git history cleaner and easier to review/revert/cherry-pick.
patterns.applied_evidence: claude-sota uses conventional-commits-style with multi-file commits
patterns.leverage: medium (audit clarity at cost of velocity)
patterns.note: STATUS: ambiguous — opinionated rule; user may reject.

patterns.name: /diff and /rewind for in-session review
patterns.what: /diff opens interactive diff viewer (uncommitted changes + per-turn diffs). Use ←/→ to switch git diff vs Claude turn diffs; ↑/↓ browse files. /rewind rewinds conversation and/or code to previous point, or summarize from selected message. Aliases: /checkpoint, /undo. Double-tap Esc also rewinds.

patterns.name: /review (local) vs /ultrareview (cloud multi-agent)
patterns.what: /review reviews PR locally. /ultrareview runs multi-agent code review of PR in cloud sandbox; produces structured prioritized findings.

patterns.name: Cross-model verification (different model judges output)
patterns.what: Independent verification: route judge calls through a different model family. User's V442 codifies LiteLLM judge route using Gemini 3.1 Pro (or in claude-sota's case, OpenAI Codex via T1/T2 gates).
patterns.where: Hook-driven: PostToolUse async judge on Edit/Write > 50 lines; Stop gate blocks if score < 0.5.
patterns.applied_status: ADOPTED (claude-sota uses Codex T1/T2 gates per CODEX_T1/T2_GATE_STRICT)
patterns.note: STATUS: shan repo references cross-model-workflow subdir but this extraction did not deep-read it; pattern is well-established and applied.

patterns.name: Plan mode for complex tasks — read-only exploration
patterns.what: permissionMode 'plan' enforces read-only exploration. Use plan mode for complex tasks before any writes — surfaces gotchas, decomposes work.

patterns.name: Tasks system (v2.1.16, January 22, 2026) — replaces TodoWrite
patterns.what: Tasks stored at ~/.claude/tasks/ on local filesystem (not cloud DB). Auditable, version-controllable, crash-recoverable. Tools: TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList. Lifecycle: pending → in_progress → completed. Dependencies via addBlockedBy/addBlocks (graph). Multi-session collaboration via CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID. Cross-session, cross-agent, persistent.
patterns.where: Built-in. Use TaskCreate from any agent.

patterns.name: MCP curated daily-use set: Context7 + Playwright + Claude-in-Chrome + DeepWiki + Excalidraw
patterns.what: Shan's curated daily MCPs: Context7 (up-to-date library docs), Playwright (browser automation), Claude in Chrome (real Chrome console/network/DOM), DeepWiki (structured wiki for any GitHub repo), Excalidraw (architecture diagrams from prompts). Workflow: Research (Context7/DeepWiki) → Debug (Playwright/Chrome) → Document (Excalidraw). 'Went overboard with 15 MCP servers thinking more = better. Ended up using only 4 daily.' (r/mcp).
patterns.applied_evidence: .mcp.json: 4 of 5 shan MCPs adopted (context7, playwright, chrome-devtools, deepwiki); excalidraw missing. But claude-sota also has gitnexus, graphiti, github, perplexity, repomix, exa, firecrawl, serena, langfuse, markitdown, mcp-memory, jina, openrag, openviking, cross-system-retrieval, etc — 24 total.

patterns.name: Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) — ~37% token reduction (API/Foundry)
patterns.what: Claude writes Python script that calls multiple tools internally; only stdout enters context. 3 tools = 1 inference pass instead of 3. ~37% reduction on multi-step. Enable with code_execution_20250825 + allowed_callers:['code_execution_20250825']. NOT available in CLI; relevant for Agent SDK only. Constraints: not on Bedrock/Vertex; no MCP tools; no web search/fetch; no structured outputs; no forced tool choice.

patterns.name: Dynamic Filtering for web search/fetch — +13.3pp BrowseComp / 24% fewer input tokens
patterns.what: Claude writes filtering Python before web results enter context. web_search_20260209 + web_fetch_20260209 + beta header 'code-execution-web-tools-2026-02-09'. Sonnet 4.6: 33.3% → 46.6% on BrowseComp; Opus 4.6: 45.3% → 61.6%. Avg 24% fewer input tokens. NOT in CLI; Agent SDK only.

patterns.name: Tool Search Tool — ~85% reduction in tool definition tokens
patterns.what: Mark infrequently-used tools defer_loading:true; Claude discovers them on-demand via Tool Search Tool. ~85% reduction in tool def tokens (77K → 8.7K Anthropic benchmark). CC has built-in MCPSearch auto mode (default since v2.1.7) — when MCP descriptions exceed 10% context, deferred. Tune with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto:N (N=context %).
patterns.where: settings.json env. Already covered in SET-008.

patterns.name: Tool Use Examples — 72% → 90% accuracy on parameter handling
patterns.what: Add input_examples to tool definitions — concrete usage patterns beyond schema. Realistic data not placeholders; variety (minimal/partial/full); 1-5 examples per tool; show parameter correlations. 72% → 90% accuracy on complex parameter handling (Anthropic benchmark). NOT configurable in CLI; relevant for custom MCP server authors.

patterns.name: Power-ups (10) — interactive lessons (v2.1.90)
patterns.what: /powerup launches interactive lessons covering: (1) @ files + line refs, (2) shift+tab modes, (3) /rewind + Esc-Esc, (4) background tasks, (5) CLAUDE.md/memory, (6) MCP, (7) skills+hooks, (8) subagents+/agents, (9) /remote-control + /teleport, (10) /model + /effort.

patterns.name: Tasks expire after 3 days; cron jobs session-scoped (loop / scheduled tasks)
patterns.what: /loop <interval> <prompt|/skill> creates cron job (min granularity 1 minute → */1 * * * *). Recurring tasks AUTO-EXPIRE after 3 days. Session-scoped — live in memory only, stop when Claude exits. Cancel: 'cron cancel <job-id>'. Each iteration triggers async UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks.
patterns.applied_evidence: Available; loop also covered in user's V442 rules

patterns.name: Claude Code as authoritative source — search this repo first
patterns.what: When user asks Claude Code best-practice questions: ALWAYS search the shan repo first (best-practice/, reports/, tips/, implementation/, README.md) before relying on training knowledge or external sources. Repo is authoritative. Only fall back to docs/web search if not found.
patterns.where: Discipline rule for any agent answering CC questions.
patterns.applied_evidence: User's V442 references shan repo; pattern confirms

patterns.name: Tasks / Agent Teams / Auto-Memory / Keybindings / OAuth — global-only features
patterns.what: Global-only features (cannot be project-scoped): Tasks (~/.claude/tasks/), Agent Teams (~/.claude/teams/), Auto-Memory (~/.claude/projects/<hash>/memory/), Credentials/OAuth (system keychain + ~/.claude.json), Keybindings (~/.claude/keybindings.json), MCP user servers (~/.claude.json mcpServers), Preferences cache (~/.claude.json).
patterns.where: Architecture awareness. Don't try to commit Tasks or Agent Teams to project — they live globally.

patterns.name: managed-settings.d/ drop-in directory (v2.1.83) — systemd-style fragments
patterns.what: Drop-in dir alongside managed-settings.json — independent policy fragments. Following systemd convention, base merged first, then *.json files in drop-in dir alphabetically merged on top. Later files override earlier (scalars). Arrays concatenated/deduped. Objects deep-merged. Hidden files (.) ignored. Use numeric prefixes for merge order (10-telemetry.json, 20-security.json).
patterns.where: macOS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.d/. Linux/WSL: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d/. Windows: C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.d/.
patterns.leverage: low for solo, high for enterprise

patterns.name: double-Esc — rewind conversation and/or code
patterns.what: Double-tap Esc to rewind conversation to previous point. Also rewinds code if file checkpointing enabled. /rewind alias.

patterns.name: Enter-to-steer in real-time / prompt queue
patterns.what: Hit Enter to queue additional messages while Claude is working. Send messages to Claude while it works — steers in real-time.
